liquids.name: Red wine
liquids.description: A dry red at about 13% alcohol: a little lighter than water, a third less surface tension, half again as viscous.

provenance.density_kgm3: published: dry red wines 990-996 kg/m3 at 20 C (OIV Compendium of International Methods, density and specific gravity)
provenance.surface_tension_mNm: published: 12-14% v/v ethanol in water, 46-49 mN/m at 20 C (Vazquez, Alvarez & Navaza, J. Chem. Eng. Data 40 (1995) 611)
provenance.viscosity_mPas: published: 12-14% v/v ethanol-water 1.5-1.7 mPa s at 20 C (Khattab et al., J. Mol. Liq. 2012); wine solids add a little
provenance.stain_color: gameplay: rendering colour of a dried red wine stain

liquids.name: White wine
liquids.description: A dry white: the same physics as the red, a pale straw colour.

provenance.density_kgm3: published: dry white wines 988-994 kg/m3 at 20 C (OIV Compendium)
provenance.surface_tension_mNm: published: 12% v/v ethanol in water ~47 mN/m (Vazquez et al. 1995)
provenance.viscosity_mPas: published: 12% v/v ethanol-water ~1.5 mPa s at 20 C

liquids.name: Water
liquids.description: Pure water at 20 C, the reference liquid of the validation cases.

provenance.density_kgm3: published: CRC Handbook of Chemistry and Physics, 998.21 kg/m3 at 20 C
provenance.surface_tension_mNm: published: IAPWS (2014) release on the surface tension of ordinary water, 72.74 mN/m at 20 C
provenance.viscosity_mPas: published: CRC Handbook, 1.0016 mPa s at 20 C
provenance.stain_color: gameplay: rendering colour of a wet mark

liquids.name: Olive oil
liquids.description: Eighty times as viscous as water: it pours in a rope and barely splashes.

provenance.density_kgm3: published: olive oil 910-916 kg/m3 at 20 C (Codex Alimentarius CXS 33-1981)
provenance.surface_tension_mNm: published: olive oil ~32 mN/m at 20 C (Sahasrabudhe et al., J. Am. Oil Chem. Soc. 2017)
provenance.viscosity_mPas: published: olive oil ~84 mPa s at 20 C (Kim et al., Int. J. Food Prop. 2010)

liquids.name: Green stage blood
liquids.description: Stage blood dyed green to keep it G-rated, with the density, surface tension and shear-thinning of whole human blood, so its spatter flies and stains like the real thing.

provenance.density_kgm3: published: whole blood 1050-1065 kg/m3 (Kenner, Basic Res. Cardiol. 84 (1989) 111)
provenance.surface_tension_mNm: published: whole blood ~56 mN/m at 37 C (Hrncir & Rosina, Physiol. Res. 46 (1997) 319)
provenance.mu0_mPas: published: Carreau fit to whole blood, mu0 = 56 mPa s (Cho & Kensey, Biorheology 28 (1991) 241)
provenance.mu_inf_mPas: published: Carreau fit, mu_inf = 3.45 mPa s (Cho & Kensey 1991)
provenance.lambda_s: published: Carreau fit, lambda = 3.313 s (Cho & Kensey 1991)
provenance.color: gameplay: green dye for a G rating
provenance.stain_color: gameplay: rendering colour of a dried stain

provenance.youngs_GPa: published: porcelain stoneware 50-70 GPa (ISO 10545 data; Dondi et al., J. Eur. Ceram. Soc. 2005)
provenance.absorbency: published: glazed surface, water absorption < 0.5% (ISO 13006 group BIa)
provenance.hysteresis: estimated: water on glazed tile, receding ~30 deg, advancing ~55 deg (contact-angle hysteresis reviews, de Gennes 1985)

surfaces.name: Oak floorboards
surfaces.description: Lacquered hardwood: the glass lands across the grain.

provenance.youngs_GPa: estimated: red oak E_L 12.5 GPa with E_R/E_L 0.15 and E_T/E_L 0.08 (USDA Wood Handbook FPL-GTR-282, table 5-1); radial-tangential mean
provenance.absorbency: estimated: lacquer seals most of it

surfaces.name: Oak table top
surfaces.description: The table the glass stands on.

surfaces.name: Polished concrete
surfaces.description: Garage or loft floor: hard and a little rough.

provenance.youngs_GPa: published: normal-weight concrete 25-35 GPa (Eurocode 2, table 3.1, C30/37: 33 GPa)
provenance.splash_factor: estimated: rougher than tile, splashes earlier (Range & Feuillebois, J. Colloid Interface Sci. 203 (1998) 16)
provenance.hysteresis: estimated: porous, rough surfaces pin more

surfaces.name: Cut-pile carpet
surfaces.description: Cut pile on a foam underlay over concrete: it catches the glass and drinks the wine.

provenance.youngs_GPa: estimated: effective compressive modulus of cut pile, ~0.3 MPa (carpet compression curves, ISO 3416)
provenance.layer_mm: estimated: 8 mm pile on a 6 mm underlay, typical residential
provenance.hysteresis: estimated: the fibres hold the liquid where it lands

surfaces.name: Painted plasterboard
surfaces.description: An interior wall with matt emulsion.

provenance.youngs_GPa: published: gypsum board 2-3 GPa (Gypsum Association GA-235)
provenance.absorbency: estimated: matt paint takes up a little

surfaces.name: Window glass
surfaces.description: Float glass: the smoothest surface here; drops spread and run rather than splash.

provenance.splash_factor: estimated: smooth glass raises the splash threshold (Xu, Zhang & Nagel, PRL 94 (2005) 184505)
provenance.hysteresis: estimated: clean float glass wets well with little hysteresis

surfaces.name: Glassware
surfaces.description: The vessel's own glass, for its pieces striking each other and the liquid wetting it.

surfaces.name: Dummy skin
surfaces.description: The crash dummy's vinyl skin over its flesh simulant.

provenance.youngs_GPa: estimated: PVC skin over urethane flesh, a few MPa

vessels.name: Bordeaux wine glass
vessels.description: A machine-made soda-lime red wine glass: tall bowl, 1.2 mm wall, solid stem, 80 mm foot.

provenance.profile_mm: estimated: drawn to a common machine-made Bordeaux glass (height 220 mm, bowl 95 mm, foot 80 mm, 1.1-1.3 mm wall)
provenance.strength_MPa: calibrated: Weibull scale for the few square millimetres a strike bends, set so that a 0.3 m/s knock on a table never breaks the glass, tipping it over sometimes does, a 0.75 m fall onto tile always does and onto carpet rarely (docs/validation.md); fire-polished soda-lime glass is far stronger over small areas than large-area design values of 50-100 MPa (Quinn, NIST SP 960-16; size effect m = 6)
provenance.weibull_modulus: published: annealed soda-lime glass m = 5-8 (Quinn 2007; ASTM C1239 practice)
provenance.capacity_ml: estimated: brimful capacity of the profile, checked by the tests
provenance.fill_ml: published: a standard pour, 5 US fl oz = 148 ml (NIAAA standard drink)

vessels.name: Bordeaux wine bottle
vessels.description: A 750 ml Bordeaux bottle: 305 mm tall, 75 mm body, 3 mm wall, heavy punted base, opened.

provenance.profile_mm: estimated: drawn to the common 750 ml Bordeaux bottle (height 295-305 mm, body 74-76 mm, punt 15-20 mm)
provenance.strength_MPa: estimated: container glass carries handling flaws from the line and the shop, so a little weaker than the stemware above
provenance.capacity_ml: published: brimful capacity of a 750 ml bottle is ~765-775 ml (OIV / EU directive 75/107/EEC measuring container tolerances)
provenance.fill_ml: estimated: a bottle opened and a glass poured

projectiles.name: 9 mm FMJ
projectiles.description: 124 grain full metal jacket from a pistol.

provenance.diameter_mm: published: C.I.P. 9 mm Luger bullet 9.01 mm
provenance.speed_ms: published: 124 gr FMJ from a 4 in barrel, 350-370 m/s (manufacturers' tables)
provenance.cd_tissue: estimated: non-yawing round-nose bullet in gelatin, 0.25-0.35 (Peters, J. Trauma 1990; Sturdivan 1978 drag fits)

provenance.speed_ms: published: 240 gr from a 6 in barrel, ~440 m/s
provenance.cd_tissue: estimated: flat meplat, more drag than round nose

projectiles.name: 7.62 x 51 mm ball
projectiles.description: 147 grain M80 ball from a rifle.

provenance.speed_ms: published: M80 from a 22 in barrel, ~840 m/s
provenance.cd_tissue: estimated: spitzer before it yaws; the yaw that real rifle rounds develop after 10-20 cm of tissue is not modelled

projectiles.name: 12-gauge 00 buckshot
projectiles.description: A 2-3/4 in 12-gauge shell of nine 8.4 mm lead balls, cylinder bore.

provenance.mass_g: published: 00 buck pellet 0.33 in (8.38 mm), 53.8 gr (3.49 g); 9 per 2-3/4 in 12-gauge shell
provenance.speed_ms: published: 1,325 ft/s (404 m/s) muzzle for standard 00 buck loads; about 395 m/s a few metres out
provenance.cd_tissue: estimated: a sphere in gelatin; with the dummy's Poncelet resistance a pellet penetrates 0.33 m (FBI-protocol tests of 00 buck report 0.35-0.45 m)
provenance.glass_impactor: gameplay: one pellet of Glass Dynamics' buckshot_00 (the host fires each pellet on its own)
provenance.pellets: published: nine pellets in a standard 2-3/4 in 00 buck shell
provenance.spread_mrad: estimated: a cylinder-bore pattern of about 1 in per yard (as Glass Dynamics' buckshot_00)
provenance.shot_string_m: estimated: shot string of a few tens of centimetres at short range (as Glass Dynamics)

dummies.name: Crash dummy
dummies.description: A generic 50th-percentile adult crash dummy (1.75 m), yellow vinyl, filled with green stage blood.

provenance.segments_m: estimated: capsules fitted to 50th-percentile adult male stature, chest breadth and depth (ANSUR II summary statistics)
provenance.tissue_density_kgm3: published: 10% ballistic gelatin and soft tissue ~1040-1060 kg/m3
provenance.tissue_strength_MPa: calibrated: Poncelet resistance R in m dv/dx = -(R A + rho Cd A v^2 / 2), set so that a 9 mm 124 gr FMJ at 360 m/s penetrates 0.65 m of 10% gelatin (FBI-protocol tests report 0.6-0.75 m)
provenance.back_spatter: estimated: back spatter is a small volume of fine drops (most under 1 mm) thrown back towards the shooter at up to ~20 m/s, as filmed by Comiskey, Yarin, Kim & Attinger (Forensic Sci. Int. 2016-2019); volume per joule, size distribution and cone are orders of magnitude, not fits
provenance.forward_spatter: estimated: forward spatter carries more liquid in larger and faster drops than back spatter (Comiskey et al. 2017-2019, Kabaliuk et al. 2014); volume per joule, size distribution and cone are orders of magnitude, not fits
provenance.bleed_ml_per_s: estimated: a slow drip from each wound after the shot, for passive drip stains
provenance.mass_kg: published: Hybrid III 50th-percentile adult male dummy, 78.2 kg (49 CFR 572 subpart E)
